links.outcome: Self-reported professional competence with structured GAI training covering risks, verification, ethics
links.effect: Structured training associated with improved self-reported competence (AOR 22.2, 95% CI 1.6–305.6, p=0.021; n=15, exploratory); any training AOR 1.98 (1.37–2.86); 86.7% vs 28.6% prioritized critical appraisal skills (OR 16.3).
links.quote: Multivariate analysis adjusted for demographic factors revealed a significant association between structured training and perceived improvement in self-reported professional competence (AOR = 22.2, 95% CI: 1.6–305.6, p = 0.021).

links.outcome: Proportion of GAI-using physicians who received formal training
links.effect: GAI usage rose from 64.7% to 94.1% while formal training stayed at 13.2% vs 13.7% (p=0.84); only 29.4% of trained received structured training.
links.quote: Despite near-universal GAI adoption (94.1%, 350/372) among post-DeepSeek respondents, participation in formal training remained disproportionately low at only 13.7% ( n = 51).

links.outcome: Self-reported improvement in professional competence associated with GAI training
links.effect: Any GAI training was associated with enhanced self-reported competence: AOR = 1.98, 95% CI: 1.37–2.86, p < 0.001. This was an observational association, not objectively measured competency improvement.
links.quote: General participation in any GAI training was associated with nearly double the odds of reporting enhanced self-reported professional competence (AOR = 1.98, 95% CI: 1.37–2.86, p < 0.001) ( Table 4 ).

links.outcome: Self-reported professional competence following structured GAI training incorporating safety and ethical content
links.effect: Structured training (n = 15) was associated with improved self-reported competence: AOR = 22.2, 95% CI: 1.6–305.6, p = 0.021. The small subgroup and wide interval make this exploratory, not causal evidence.
links.quote: Multivariate analysis adjusted for demographic factors revealed a significant association between structured training and perceived improvement in self-reported professional competence (AOR = 22.2, 95% CI: 1.6–305.6, p = 0.021).

links.effect: 86.7% of physicians with structured training prioritized critical integration skills, compared to 28.6% without such training
links.quote: When asked about the important physician skills for applying GAI in critical care, 86.7% (13/15) of the physicians with structured training identified critical integration skills (critical appraisal or clinical reasoning integration) as the primary competency, compared to only 28.6% (102/357) of those without such training.
